subject: RE: CI/CD runner licensing and registry retention — decision path
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-28T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: CI/CD runner renewal + registry retention — heads up

Soojin / Marissa,

We have the Buildkite contract coming up for renewal in early December (self-hosted runner licenses + support). Separately, GCP Artifact Registry retention and tiered storage charges are being bumped for large container layers (our estimates for Q1 2027).

Key asks:
- Confirm whether we move to a multi-year committed license for Buildkite self-hosted runners or switch to their managed offering for a subset of pipelines. Rough cost delta is in the runbook (attached).
- Decide on a retention policy: keep 90 days for images vs move to 30/60 day tiers and archive older layers to cold storage. 
- Identify who should engage Buildkite sales and GCP for negotiated terms (SLA, transfer pricing, egress).

I attached a quick cost model (runbook_cost_model.xlsx) with usage by repo and runner-hours. Please advise by next Tue 11/2 so Procurement can start negotiations.

Thanks,
Dev

Thanks Dev — and looping in Emma from Buildkite so we can get options on managed vs committed runner pricing.

Marissa — I'm leaning toward: 1) committing to a 12-month license for baseline capacity to get a better unit price, and 2) piloting Buildkite's managed runners for a few high-concurrency repos to simplify ops. If Buildkite can guarantee predictable burst capacity and a fallback SLA, that reduces our ops cost.

On the registry side, I want GCP retention numbers before we decide archive vs shorter retention. Oliver from GCP can share the cost breakouts.

Emma — can you send a short proposal (two options):
- Option A: 12mo committed self-hosted runner licenses with X reserved concurrency + support (include discount tiers)
- Option B: Hybrid — lower committed baseline + managed runners for up to 25% of peak load (include SLA and estimated per-minute charges)

Please include lead times, any professional services for migration to managed runners, and redlines for permissible early-termination credits.

Dev / Marissa — we'll review Emma's note and then schedule a 30-min sync with Procurement next week.

Soojín Lee
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Green <emma@buildkite.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CI/CD runner renewal + registry retention — proposal options

Hi Soojin / Dev —

Thanks for the context. Attached is a short proposal with two pricing options as requested and an outline of migration steps for the hybrid approach. High-level summary below:

Option A — Committed Self-hosted Runners (12mo)
- Reserved runner licenses for 120 concurrent workers; 18% discount vs monthly
- 24/7 standard support; optional on-call escalation at additional fee
- No changes to our agent tooling; no migration cost

Option B — Hybrid (Baseline + Managed Burst)
- Baseline reserved licenses for 80 concurrent workers; managed runners available for burst up to +40 concurrent workers at $0.052/min
- Guaranteed managed-runner SLA: 99.5% availability on worker allocation within 2 mins for burst requests
- One-week POC to validate perf and caching behavior; PS engagement estimated at 20 engineer-hours

We find most customers save ~12-25% in ops cost when moving non-sensitive workloads to managed runners due to reduced infra maintenance and better autoscaling.

Attached: Buildkite_proposal_Redwood_Nov2026.pdf

Happy to jump on a call and walk the team through the numbers.

Best,
Emma Green
Enterprise Sales, Buildkite
[Attachment: Buildkite_proposal_Redwood_Nov2026.pdf (pdf)]

From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@gcp-artifactsales.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: GCP Artifact Registry retention tiers and pricing

Soojín / Dev —

Following up with the retention/pricing spreadsheet you requested. Short summary:
- Standard (default): 90-day retention included in base storage pricing.
- Nearline archive: 180/365-day cold tier with lower storage cost but retrieval fees on access.
- Layer dedup and egress: aggressive dedup across manifests reduces incremental storage by ~10-15% for multi-arch images.

If Redwood locks in a 12-month committed spend for Artifact Registry (minimum $45k/year), we can offer a 10% discount on storage rates and waive retrieval fees for one free restore per month.

Attached: GCP_artifact_retention_pricing.csv

If you want, we can set up a short call with the technical account manager to discuss dedup and lifecycle rules.

Regards,
Oliver Park
GCP Artifact Registry — Strategic Accounts
[Attachment: GCP_artifact_retention_pricing.csv (csv)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Emma Green <emma@buildkite.com>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@gcp-artifactsales.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T16:24:00-08:00
Subject: RE: CI/CD runner licensing and registry retention — decision path

Thanks everyone for the quick turn. Summary and next steps: 

Decision (tentative):
- Buildkite: move forward with Option B (Hybrid) — reserved baseline for 80 concurrent self-hosted runners + managed-runner burst for non-sensitive pipelines. Procurement to negotiate the per-minute burst cap and a 10% discount on the POC/PS hours.
- Artifact Registry: pursue 12-month committed spend to capture the 10% discount and waived single monthly restore; set lifecycle rules to 60-day active retention + archive older manifests to nearline.

Action owners and deadlines:
- Procurement (Dev): open negotiation ticket with Buildkite and GCP; target final terms by 2026-11-17. (Deal id BK-2026-09-REDW-01)
- Platform (Marissa): pick three candidate repos for the managed-runner POC and provide test corpus by 2026-11-10.
- Buildkite (Emma): send final contract draft with explicit burst pricing caps and early-termination credits by 2026-11-12.
- GCP (Oliver): prepare SOW for committed spend and confirm lifecycle rule support in our project by 2026-11-12.

I'll schedule a 30-min decision review with Procurement and Finance the week of 11/15. If anyone has objections to the plan, flag them by EOD Friday 11/5.

Thanks,
Soojín
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
